Munajat-e-Maqbool

Sunday

Second manzil · supplications 55 to 85

Opening praise

In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

We praise You, O best of those in whom hope is placed and most generous of those from whom anything is sought, for teaching us Munajat-e-Maqbool, which brings nearness to Allah, and the supplications of the Messenger. Send perfect blessings upon him for as long as the west and east winds blow, and branches spring from their roots. Then we ask You for what we are about to recite. Ours is to ask, and Yours is to grant acceptance.

How to read

Read this opening invocation before each daily portion. Begin on Saturday, read one portion each day in order, and complete the cycle on Friday.

Swipe right to left to turn the page

In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

Supplication55

Help, gratitude, repentance and a purified heart

My Lord, help me and do not help anyone against me. Grant me victory and do not grant victory over me. Plan in my favour and do not plan against me. Guide me, make guidance easy for me, and grant me victory over whoever wrongs me. My Lord, make me one who remembers You often, thanks You abundantly, fears You greatly, and is eager to obey You, obedient to You, humble before You, earnest in supplication to You, and constantly turning to You.

My Lord, accept my repentance, wash away my sins, answer my prayer, make my proof firm, set my tongue straight, guide my heart, and remove the rancour from my breast.

Original commentary 55

This long supplication asks: O Allah, help me, protect me from anyone who oppresses or wrongs me, and grant me Your help. Accept my repentance, forgive my sins, set my tongue straight, grant guidance to my heart, and accept my prayer. Enable me to remember You and give thanks to You.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 35 · Combination of hadith variants

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3551

Component: The complete prayer, with differences in the obedience and humility phrases. Al-Tirmidhi: hasan sahih. The report contains mitwaʿan, laka mukhbitan, and sakhimata sadri. It places gratitude before remembrance and has no separate mutiʿan.

Sunan Ibn Majah 3830

Component: The alternate words mutiʿan and ilayka mukhbitan within the same supplication. Not independently assessed here; compare the graded Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud recensions. This recension has mutiʿan and ilayka mukhbitan, rather than both obedience terms together. Its last clause refers to the heart.

Sunan Abi Dawud 1510

Variant: The supplication as a whole, with recension differences. Al-Albani: sahih. The inspected report supplies an authenticated parallel recension of this long prayer.

The compilation combines wording from different recensions, including both mitwaʿan and mutiʿan, and changes their order. All substantive requests are traced, but the assembled wording is not one verbatim quotation from the cited reports.

Supplication56

Forgiveness, mercy and all affairs put right

O Allah, forgive us, have mercy on us, be pleased with us, admit us to Paradise, save us from the Fire, and set all our affairs right.

Original commentary 56

This supplication teaches us to ask for mercy, forgiveness and Allah's pleasure. It ends with a remarkably concise and comprehensive phrase that should always be on the tongue, asking Allah to set all our affairs right.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 36 · Hadith excerpt from a weak report

Sunan Ibn Majah 3836

Excerpt: All requests; the compilation omits the request for acceptance. Darussalam: daʿif. The primary Arabic contains the printed sequence and additionally wa-taqabbal minna.

The supplication is traceable to a report graded weak by Darussalam. It is a transmitted prayer with a qualified attribution; the located report does not support an unqualified claim of authentic Prophetic wording.

Supplication57

United hearts, peace and blessings for the family

O Allah, unite our hearts, put our relationships right, guide us along the paths of peace, deliver us from darkness into light, and keep us away from shameful deeds, both open and hidden. Bless our hearing, our sight, our hearts, our spouses and our offspring. Accept our repentance, for You are the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful. Make us grateful for Your favour, praising You for it and accepting it, and perfect it for us.

Original commentary 57

This supplication is a potent prescription for creating love and harmony among Muslims. It is a prayer for dispelling darkness and attaining light. These words should be on the tongue at all times. This supplication teaches us to pray: O Allah, bless our home, grant every kind of good to our wives and children, and bless our eyes and our ears.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 37 · Hadith exact

Sunan Abi Dawud 969

Exact. Al-Albani: sahih. The inspected Arabic gives the whole sequence, including the final requests to receive, praise and complete Allah’s blessing.

The full prayer is located in the cited report. The devotional commentary about harmony is an explanation of its requests, not a fixed reward.

Supplication58

Steadfastness, gratitude and upright character

O Allah, I ask You for steadfastness in religion, and I ask You for firm resolve in righteousness. I ask You for gratitude for Your favour and excellence in worshipping You. I ask You for a truthful tongue, a sound heart and upright character. I ask You for the good that You know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what You know. Surely You are the Knower of all unseen things.

Original commentary 58

This supplication teaches us to ask: O Allah, grant us steadfastness in all matters of religion. I ask You for a truthful tongue and the ability to give thanks in the best way. It also teaches us to pray: O Allah, make me grateful for the blessings You have bestowed upon me. Above all, it teaches this prayer: O Allah, grant me a truthful tongue.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 38 · Combination of hadith variants

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3407

Component: Steadfastness, resolve, gratitude, worship, truthful tongue, sound heart and the concluding requests. Darussalam: hasan. The report covers these clauses but does not contain khuluqan mustaqiman. It also contains a request for refuge omitted by the compilation.

Al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 1872 (also numbered 1896)

Locator: 1872 / 1896. Component: The fuller variant, including upright character. Al-Hakim: sahih on Muslim’s conditions. The primary-source text explicitly includes wa-khuluqan mustaqiman alongside the sound heart and truthful tongue.

The requests are all traceable across recensions. The order is adjusted and some phrases are omitted. The request for upright character is present in the fuller al-Hakim recension and absent from Tirmidhi 3407.

Supplication59

Forgiveness, reverence and protection of religion

O Allah, forgive me for what I have done earlier and later, for what I have concealed and what I have made known, and for what You know better than I do. O Allah, grant us such fear of You as will come between us and disobedience to You; such obedience to You as will bring us to Your Paradise; and such certainty as will make the hardships of this world easy for us.

Let us benefit from our hearing and our sight and our strength for as long as You keep us alive, and let these remain with us to the end. Direct our retribution against those who have wronged us, and grant us victory over those who are hostile to us. Do not let our misfortune be in our religion. Do not make this world our greatest concern, the limit of our knowledge or the furthest aim of our desire. Do not place over us anyone who has no mercy on us.

Original commentary 59

This supplication describes the proper measure of fear and awe of Allah. It means: O Allah, grant us only such fear as will stand between us and disobedience, and grant us such servitude as will become a means of reaching Paradise. Bestow upon us such certainty in Your Being that whatever hardship befalls us afterwards seems easy to us. Furthermore, in this comprehensive supplication, we are also taught to pray: O Allah, protect my religion. Do not let any trial or calamity afflict my religion. Do not make the world our ultimate purpose or the final limit of our knowledge. Take retribution on our behalf against anyone who oppresses or wrongs us, and grant us victory over those who are hostile to us. Do not place over us anyone who is cruel and merciless; that is, do not appoint over us a ruler who is not compassionate, kind and sympathetic towards us.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 39 · Composite of reports and recensions; one variant not graded here

Sahih Muslim 2719a

Component: Opening request for forgiveness of earlier, later, hidden and public deeds and what Allah knows better. Sahih: included by Muslim in his Sahih. The opening is an excerpt from Ali’s longer prayer.

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3502

Component: The prayer beginning Allahumma iqsim lana, except the added furthest aim of our desire clause. Al-Tirmidhi: hasan gharib; Darussalam: sahih. The report has ma yahulu and musibat al-dunya variants. It proceeds from the limit of our knowledge directly to protection from merciless people; wa-la ghayata raghbatina is absent.

Al-Shajari, al-Amali al-Khamisiyya, Ibn Umar report (Tartib numbering 1099)

Locator: Ibn Umar report; Tartib 1099. Component: The added clause wa-la ghayata raghbatina. Not assessed: no specific named grading verified for this additional wording and route. The primary collection text contains the full chain through Ibn al-Mubarak, Yahya ibn Ayyub, Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr and Khalid ibn Abi Imran, and explicitly includes this clause.

The opening and the main prayer come from different reports. The additional clause wa-la ghayata raghbatina is absent from Tirmidhi 3502 but occurs in al-Shajari’s al-Amali al-Khamisiyya. Its presence in that source establishes traceability, not an independent authenticity grade; Tirmidhi’s grading does not cover this extra wording. The commentary’s only such fear is interpretive: the prayer asks for fear sufficient to prevent disobedience, without imposing an upper limit on reverence.

Supplication60

Increase, honour, provision and contentment

O Allah, increase us and do not diminish us; honour us and do not humiliate us; give to us and do not deprive us; favour us and do not favour others over us; make us content and be pleased with us.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 41 · Hadith exact, grading disputed

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3173

Exact. Not graded independently here; see the differing named assessments below. The primary Arabic contains the complete short prayer in the report concerning the opening of Surah al-Mu’minun.

Al-Albani, Daʿif al-Jami 1208; al-Nasai, al-Sunan al-Kubra 1439

Locator: 1208 / 1439. Exact. Al-Albani: daʿif; al-Nasai calls the report munkar and identifies Yunus ibn Sulaym as unknown. The source excerpt records al-Nasai’s criticism of the route, in addition to the later weak grading.

Al-Suyuti, al-Jami al-Saghir 1461

Exact. Al-Suyuti: sahih. This named assessment differs from al-Albani’s and al-Nasai’s criticism.

The wording is located, but its attribution is disputed. The differing named assessments are set out above; the report is not established here as an unqualified authenticated Prophetic prayer.

Supplication61

Inspiration toward right guidance

O Allah, inspire me with right guidance.

Original commentary 61

This magnificent supplication is a prayer for guidance and inspiration at every turn of life. Hakim al-Ummah, Mawlana Muhammad Ashraf Ali Thanawi, may Allah have mercy on him, made a remarkable statement about it. He said: 'Throughout my life, before doing any work, I have recited this supplication.' He then said: 'I cannot remember ever reciting it, making a decision, and then regretting that decision.'

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 41 · Hadith excerpt, grading disputed

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3483

Excerpt. Al-Tirmidhi: hasan gharib; Darussalam: daʿif. The short request is the first half of the prayer taught to Husayn; the other half seeks protection from the evil of the self.

The quoted report has differing assessments. The commentary’s recollection about Mawlana Ashraf Ali Thanawi is a personal devotional testimony in the source book, not a Prophetic guarantee that every subsequent decision will be free of regret.

Supplication62

Protection from the self and resolve for right conduct

O Allah, protect me from the evil of my own self, and grant me firm resolve to put my affairs right.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 41 · Hadith variant

Al-Nasai, al-Sunan al-Kubra 10830; Ahmad 19992

Locator: 10830 / 19992. Variant. Shuʿayb al-Arnaut: Ahmad’s chain is sahih on the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim. The primary Nasai excerpt has ʿala rushdi amri as in the book. The parallel Ahmad wording has arshada amri; the cited chain assessment belongs to Ahmad’s report.

The precise printed wording is found in the Nasai recension. The cited chain assessment belongs to the corresponding Ahmad route and does not automatically apply to a different edition or chain.

Supplication63

Well-being in this world and the Hereafter

I ask Allah for well-being in this world and the Hereafter.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 42 · Adaptation of a Prophetic instruction

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3514

Variant. Al-Tirmidhi: sahih; Darussalam: sahih. The Prophet instructs al-Abbas to ask Allah for well-being in this world and the Hereafter. The report uses the imperative sal Allah; the compilation uses first-person as’alu Allah.

The request follows an authenticated instruction, converted into the speaker’s own supplication. It is not a verbatim quotation of the imperative wording.

Supplication64

Good deeds, love and protection from trials

O Allah, I ask You to enable me to do good deeds, leave evil deeds and love the poor, and I ask You to forgive me and have mercy on me. When You intend a trial for a people, take me in death before I am afflicted by it. I ask You for Your love, the love of those who love You, and the love of deeds that bring me closer to Your love.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 42 · Hadith excerpt with minor variants

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3235

Variant. Al-Tirmidhi: hasan sahih; Darussalam: hasan. The full prayer is contained in the report. The compilation rearranges the words of the clause about an intended trial for a people.

All requests are supported by the cited report. The wording about death is conditional upon a destructive trial and asks to be spared being led astray by it.

Supplication65

Love of Allah above self, family and comfort

O Allah, make Your love dearer to me than my own self, my family and cool water.

Original commentary 65

This supplication asks for love of Allah Most High and love of every person who is beloved to Allah. O Allah, grant our hearts this love too.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 43 · Hadith excerpt

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3490

Excerpt. Al-Tirmidhi: hasan gharib; Darussalam: hasan. The passage is the closing request of a prayer of Dawud related by the Prophet.

The report presents the Prophet’s narration of a prayer of Dawud. The book excerpts its concluding request.

Supplication66

Loved gifts as strength for obedience

O Allah, grant me Your love and the love of those whose love will benefit me in Your sight. O Allah, whatever You have granted me of the things I love, make it a source of strength for me in doing what You love.

Original commentary 66

Likewise, enable us to do every deed that becomes a means to Your love. Whatever You have given us that is pleasing to us, make it our helper and support in all the deeds that are pleasing to You.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 43 · Hadith excerpt with minor variant, grading disputed

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3491

Variant. Al-Tirmidhi: hasan gharib; Darussalam: daʿif. The text contains this first part of the prayer; the compilation adds a connecting fa before ma razaqtani.

Numbers 66 and 67 divide a single transmitted prayer. Its grading is disputed; the Darussalam assessment is daʿif, not sahih.

Supplication67

Freedom for what Allah loves

O Allah, whatever You have withheld from me of the things I love, make that a means of freeing me for what You love.

Original commentary 67

This transmitted supplication expresses the voice of every Muslim heart. My father, Mufti Muhammad Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, used to say that these supplications of the Prophet, peace be upon him, proclaim that no one other than the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, could teach us such things. The meaning of this supplication is: O Allah, make the prayers You have accepted according to my wishes and preferences a means of attaining the things that lead to Your love. O Allah, as for those requests I desired which You have not accepted, turn my heart towards the supplications that are pleasing to You.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 44 · Hadith excerpt with minor variant, grading disputed

Jami al-Tirmidhi 3491

Variant. Al-Tirmidhi: hasan gharib; Darussalam: daʿif. The final sentence of the same prayer has li faraghan, while the book has faraghan li.

The translation of the prayer itself correctly conveys release for what Allah loves. The original commentary expands this into a discussion of answered and unanswered personal requests; that is devotional interpretation, not a literal translation of the Arabic or a separate guaranteed benefit.

Supplication68

A heart firm upon religion

O Turner of hearts, keep my heart firm upon Your religion.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 44 · Hadith exact

Jami al-Tirmidhi 2140

Exact. Al-Tirmidhi: hasan. Anas reports that the Prophet frequently said this complete short supplication.

The wording and its use as a prayer for steadfastness are directly supported by the report.

Supplication69

Unwavering faith and companionship in Paradise

O Allah, I ask You for faith that does not turn back, bliss that never ends, and the companionship of Your Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the highest rank of Paradise, the everlasting Garden.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 45 · Companion supplication with reported Prophetic approval

Ibn Abi Shayba 29531; al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 1928 (also numbered 1952)

Locator: 29531 / 1928 / 1952. Exact. Al-Hakim: sahih chain. The primary Ibn Abi Shayba excerpt contains the printed prayer. It is spoken by Ibn Masʿud; the Prophet encourages him to ask.

Ahmad 3797

Variant. Shuʿayb al-Arnaut: sahih li-ghayrihi. The parallel report uses the highest chambers rather than the highest rank and likewise identifies Ibn Masʿud as the supplicant.

The report establishes Ibn Masʿud’s supplication in the Prophet’s presence and the Prophet’s encouragement to him. It does not establish that the Prophet himself recited these exact words.

Supplication70

Health, faith, character and success

O Allah, I ask You for health accompanied by faith, faith accompanied by good character, success which You follow with prosperity, mercy from You, well-being, forgiveness from You and Your good pleasure.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 45 · Hadith variant, grading disputed

Al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 1919; al-Nasai, al-Sunan al-Kubra 9849

Locator: 1919 / 9849. Variant. Al-Hakim: sahih chain; al-Albani, Daʿif al-Jami 1195: daʿif. The primary text includes mercy, well-being, forgiveness and pleasure. It reads success followed by prosperity, whereas the compilation addresses Allah as the One who makes prosperity follow success.

The English follows the printed Arabic variant. The narrated attribution has differing named assessments, which are listed above.

Supplication71

Beneficial knowledge

O Allah, benefit me through what You have taught me, and teach me what will benefit me.

Original commentary 71

This transmitted supplication teaches us to ask Allah for knowledge that is beneficial and useful.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 46 · Hadith excerpt

Al-Nasai, al-Sunan al-Kubra 7868; al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 1879

Locator: 7868 / 1879. Excerpt. Al-Albani, al-Silsila al-Sahiha 3151: sahih on Muslim’s conditions; al-Hakim likewise. The primary Anas report contains both printed sentences and an additional request for knowledge that benefits.

The cited Anas route supplies these words. Some familiar Abu Hurayra recensions in Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah have different chain assessments; their weakness does not by itself determine the grade of this separate route.

Supplication72

Life, death, contentment and the vision of Allah

O Allah, by Your knowledge of the unseen and Your power over creation, keep me alive for as long as You know life to be better for me, and cause me to die when You know death to be better for me. I ask You for reverent fear of You in private and in public, and for sincere speech in contentment and in anger. I ask You for bliss that never runs out and joy that never ends.

I ask You for contentment with Your decree, a pleasant life after death, the delight of looking upon Your countenance and longing to meet You. I seek refuge in You from affliction that causes harm and trials that lead astray. O Allah, adorn us with the beauty of faith, and make us guides who are rightly guided.

Original commentary 72

This supplication teaches us that a person should not wish for death. Instead, one should pray in this way: O Allah, keep me alive for as long as life is better for me, and grant me death when death is better. Alongside this, the remaining requests taught in this prayer accord with human nature. That is: O Lord, after giving me death, enable me to look upon Your countenance, and grant me the ability to remain content with all Your decrees. It is an excellent prayer for attaining a good ending.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 46 · Hadith exact

Sunan al-Nasai 1306

Exact. Darussalam: hasan. This specific recension contains kalimata al-ikhlas, contentment with the decree, and the explicit refuge from harmful affliction, matching the compilation. Nasai 1305 is a different recension.

The complete printed prayer is found in Nasai 1306. Differences from Nasai 1305 reflect a different recension and do not by themselves indicate unsupported additions.

Supplication73

Every good, known and unknown

O Allah, I ask You for every good, both immediate and deferred, what I know of it and what I do not know.

Original commentary 73

This supplication teaches us to seek every good, whether near or far. It is a brief yet tremendous prayer in which every kind of good and well-being is requested.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 48 · Hadith excerpt

Sunan Ibn Majah 3846

Excerpt. Darussalam: sahih. The printed text is the opening petition of the comprehensive prayer taught to Aisha.

The excerpt is fully covered; the cited report continues with protection from evil and further requests.

Supplication74

Paradise and a good outcome for every decree

O Allah, I ask You for the good that Your servant and Your Prophet asked of You. O Allah, I ask You for Paradise and whatever brings one nearer to it, in word or deed. I ask You to make every decree concerning me good, and I ask You to make the outcome of whatever You have decreed for me rightly guided.

Original commentary 74

This supplication asks for all the good and well-being that the noble Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked of Allah. It also asks for every word and deed that is a means of attaining Paradise.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 48 · Composite of hadith recensions

Sunan Ibn Majah 3846

Component: The Prophet’s requested good; Paradise and what leads to it; a good decree. Darussalam: sahih. The printed passage selects these requests from Aisha’s longer prayer, with an abridged form of the decree clause.

Ahmad 25137

Component: The final request that the outcome of each decreed affair be rightly guided. Shuʿayb al-Arnaut: sahih chain. This recension contains the separate ending asking that the outcome of what has been decreed be rushdan.

The compilation joins two transmitted endings. Both are sourced, but the assembled prayer combines recensions rather than forming one continuous quotation from Ibn Majah.

Supplication75

A good ending and protection from disgrace

O Allah, make the outcome of all our affairs good, and protect us from disgrace in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.

Original commentary 75

Every person should learn this transmitted supplication. Its meaning is: O Allah, make the outcome of all our affairs good, and protect us from disgrace in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 49 · Hadith exact

Ahmad 17628; Ibn Hibban 949

Locator: 17628 / 949. Exact. Ahmad Shakir, ʿUmdat al-Tafsir 1/162: indicated authenticity by his stated introductory convention; Ibn Hibban included the report in his Sahih. The primary Ahmad passage gives the complete printed dua; the Ibn Hibban material includes a closely related wording and the ʿaqibatana recension.

The full prayer is located. The grading statement is the assessment of the named source, not an established scholarly consensus.

Supplication76

Preservation in Islam and Allah’s abundant good

O Allah, preserve me in Islam while standing, preserve me in Islam while sitting, and preserve me in Islam while lying down. Do not give any enemy or envious person cause to rejoice at my misfortune. O Allah, I ask You for every good whose treasures are in Your hand, and I ask You for the good that is entirely in Your hand.

Original commentary 76

This supplication asks for good and well-being in both worlds: keep us firmly attached to Islam, grant us rest while remaining in Islam, and protect us from the schemes of enemies and envious people.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 49 · Composite of hadith reports

Al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 1945 (also numbered 1924); al-Tabarani, al-Duʿa 1445

Locator: 1945 / 1924 / 1445. Component: Preservation in Islam while standing, sitting and lying down; protection from enemy gloating; good whose treasures are with Allah. Al-Albani, al-Silsila al-Sahiha 1540: hasan li-shawahidihi. The primary text reads an envious enemy, whereas the compilation separates enemy or envier. Its additional refuge from evil is omitted.

Ibn Hibban, al-Taqasim wa-l-Anwaʿ 1797; al-Bayhaqi, al-Daʿawat al-Kabir 252

Locator: 1797 / 252. Component: The closing request for the good entirely in Allah’s hand. Ibn Hibban included the report in his Sahih compilation; Ibn Kathir, Musnad al-Faruq 1/179: gharib (a description of rarity, not by itself an authenticity grade). The primary Ibn Hibban text contains wa-as’aluka min al-khayri alladhi huwa bi-yadika kullihi in a different, longer report.

Two reports have been joined. The supporting-route hasan assessment applies to the first report only; the second has its own chain and does not inherit that grade. Some individual routes of the first prayer are weak even though al-Albani strengthens it through supporting reports.

Supplication77

Forgiveness, relief, debt and every need

O Allah, leave no sin of ours unforgiven, no worry unrelieved, no debt unpaid, and no need of this world or the Hereafter unfulfilled, O Most Merciful of those who show mercy.

Original commentary 77

This supplication asks for the forgiveness of every kind of sin, deliverance from every kind of worry and distress, and freedom from every kind of debt. It gathers together all the needs of this world and the Hereafter.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 50 · Hadith excerpt from a weak report

Al-Tabarani, al-Duʿa 1044; al-Muʿjam al-Awsat 3398

Locator: 1044 / 3398. Excerpt: all, with omission of bi-rahmatika before the final address. Al-Haythami, Majmaʿ al-Zawa’id 10/160: the chain contains ʿAbbad ibn Abd al-Samad, who is weak. The primary al-Duʿa text contains the plural lana and all petitions, including debt and needs of this world and the Hereafter. The compilation omits bi-rahmatika.

Al-Haythami, Majmaʿ al-Zawa’id 10/160

Parallel only: Assessment of the Anas report supporting this wording. Al-Haythami: ʿAbbad ibn Abd al-Samad is weak. Al-Haythami’s criticism concerns the same report in al-Tabarani’s al-Muʿjam al-Awsat 3398.

The full sequence, including debt and worldly/otherworldly needs, is traced to the Tabarani report. These are sourced clauses, although the route is weak. A related Ibn Abi Awfa prayer-of-need report in Tirmidhi 479 and Ibn Majah 1384 is also weak, but is not the fullest source for this wording. The compilation does not establish a guaranteed ritual result.

Supplication78

Help in remembrance, gratitude and worship

O Allah, help us to remember You, give thanks to You and worship You well.

Original commentary 78

The noble Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to recite this transmitted supplication after the obligatory prayer. Its meaning is: O Allah, grant us the ability to remember You, give thanks to You and worship You well.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 50 · Plural adaptation of hadith wording

Sunan Abi Dawud 1522

Variant. Al-Albani: sahih. The Prophet teaches Muʿadh to say aʿinni, help me, at the conclusion of every prayer. The compilation uses aʿinna, help us.

The plural request adapts the authenticated singular. The original commentary says the Prophet used to recite it after obligatory prayer; the cited report directly establishes his instruction to Muʿadh to say it at the conclusion of prayer. This source alone does not settle every question about recitation before or after the final salam.

Supplication79

Contentment, blessing and care for what is absent

O Allah, make me content with what You have provided for me, bless it for me, and take good care of all that is absent from me.

Original commentary 79

This transmitted supplication encourages us to pray for contentment with our provision. It is beneficial for people absorbed in greed, covetousness and the accumulation of wealth.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 51 · Hadith exact, grading disputed

Al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 1878 (also numbered 1902); Ibn Khuzayma 2728

Locator: 1878 / 1902 / 2728. Exact. Al-Hakim: sahih chain. The full primary text matches the prayer; the Ibn Khuzayma recension opens Rabbi.

Ibn Hajar, quoted in Ibn Allan, al-Futuhat al-Rabbaniyya 4/383

Exact. Ibn Hajar: hasan. Ibn Allan quotes Ibn Hajar’s hasan assessment in al-Futuhat al-Rabbaniyya.

Al-Albani, al-Silsila al-Daʿifa 6042

Exact. Al-Albani: daʿif. This later chain assessment differs from those of al-Hakim and Ibn Hajar.

The wording is traceable, with a genuine difference in scholarly grading. The translation of the final clause expresses asking Allah to take good care of what is absent from the supplicant.

Supplication80

A pure life, good death and honourable return

O Allah, I ask You for a pure life, a good death and a return free from disgrace and humiliation.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 51 · Hadith exact, grading disputed

Al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 1986; al-Bayhaqi, al-Daʿawat al-Kabir 196

Locator: 1986 / 196. Exact. Al-Hakim: sahih chain; al-Albani, al-Silsila al-Daʿifa 2915: daʿif. The complete text is reproduced in the primary source; its chain has these differing assessments.

The prayer’s attribution has differing named assessments. A weak assessment of its transmission is not a judgment that its requests are impermissible as personal supplication.

Supplication81

Strength in weakness and honour through Islam

O Allah, I am weak, so strengthen my weakness in seeking Your pleasure. Take me by the forelock towards good, and make Islam the utmost object of my contentment. I am lowly, so grant me honour; I am in need, so provide for me.

Original commentary 81

In this transmitted supplication, a person pleads by mentioning their helplessness and weakness: O Allah, look upon my helplessness and, through Your special grace and kindness, lead me towards good.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 52 · Hadith excerpt from a severely weak route

Ibn Abi Shayba 29965; al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 1931

Locator: 29965 / 1931. Excerpt. Al-Haythami, Majmaʿ al-Zawa’id 10/185: the route includes Abu Dawud al-Aʿma, who is very weak; al-Hakim had called the chain sahih. The primary Ibn Abi Shayba text contains the printed clauses with an additional repeated request for strength omitted by the compilation.

The located chain has a serious weakness identified by al-Haythami. It does not securely establish Prophetic attribution or the surrounding report’s claimed protection from forgetting.

Supplication82

The best of life, deeds and the Hereafter

O Allah, I ask You for the best requests, the best supplications, the best success, the best deeds, the best reward, the best life and the best death. Make me steadfast, make my scales heavy with good deeds, make my faith firm, raise my rank and accept my prayer. I ask You for the highest ranks of Paradise. Amin. O Allah, I ask You for the beginnings and endings of good, for all that it encompasses, its first and its last, its outward and its inward aspects. O Allah, I ask You for the good of what I undertake, the good of what I do, the good of what I carry out, and the good of what is hidden and what is apparent.

Original commentary 82

This supplication asks: O Allah, when good deeds are weighed in the balance of justice on the Day of Gathering, make the pan containing my good deeds heavy. It also asks: O Allah, strengthen my faith, accept my prayers, make my beginning good and make my end good as well.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 53 · Abridged combination of hadith variants, grading disputed

Al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 1911 (also numbered 1935 or 1954); al-Tabarani, al-Duʿa 1422

Locator: 1911 / 1935 / 1954 / 1422. Variant. Al-Hakim: sahih chain. The primary texts contain the sequence of requests. The compilation abridges repeated Paradise and forgiveness petitions and combines variant wording; akhirahu is supplied by the Tabarani and Bayhaqi versions.

IslamQA scholarly review 433679

Parallel only: Chain assessment of the Umm Salama report, not an independent source of the Arabic. IslamQA review 433679: chain has weakness owing to the insufficiently established reliability of ʿAsim ibn Abi ʿUbayd. The review addresses the primary chains and earlier favourable judgments, and explains its own reservation about the narrator.

The text is located across the cited versions, but the chain assessment is disputed. Al-Hakim’s favourable assessment differs from the weak-chain reservation described above and is not an established consensus. This is an abridged version, not the full narrated prayer.

Supplication83

Abundant provision in old age

O Allah, make Your provision for me most abundant in my old age and at the close of my life.

Original commentary 83

This supplication teaches us to pray for ample and abundant provision in old age, when a person’s limbs grow weak, and in the final part of life, so that it may be a support in weakness and helplessness. It also asks: O Allah, make the day on which I meet You the best day of my life, a day of success.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 54 · Hadith exact from a very weak report

Al-Tabarani, al-Muʿjam al-Awsat 3611; al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 1987; al-Bayhaqi, al-Daʿawat al-Kabir 270

Locator: 3611 / 1987 / 270. Exact. Al-Hakim: hasan chain; al-Bayhaqi immediately identifies ʿIsa ibn Maymun as munkar al-hadith. The full primary prayer is present. The favourable Hakim assessment must be read alongside the explicit narrator criticism.

Al-Albani, al-Silsila al-Daʿifa 1385

Exact. Al-Albani: very weak. This assessment addresses the same prayer and its defective route.

Al-Albani, former Sahih al-Jami 1255, retracted assessment

Locator: 1255 / 1385. Parallel only: Correction of a frequently repeated favourable grade. Al-Albani retracted the earlier hasan assessment and requested transfer to Daʿif al-Jami; see al-Silsila al-Daʿifa 1385. Al-Albani explicitly retracted his earlier hasan assessment; his later assessment of this report is very weak.

This report is not verified here as reliably established Prophetic wording. The prayer’s meaning is distinct from the weakness of its attribution. The source’s commentary also discusses the first clause of number 84. Al-Albani retracted his earlier hasan assessment; his later assessment is very weak.

Supplication84

A good end and steadfastness until meeting Allah

Make the last part of my life its best part, the closing deeds of my life my best deeds, and the day I meet You the best of my days. O Guardian of Islam and its people, keep me steadfast in it until I meet You. I ask You [for forgiveness] for myself and those connected to me.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 54 · Composite, final clause untraced

Al-Tabarani, al-Muʿjam al-Awsat 9411; Ibn al-Sunni, ʿAmal al-Yawm wa-l-Layla 121

Locator: 9411 / 121. Component: The best of life at its end, closing deeds and the day of meeting Allah. Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Salihi, Subul al-Huda wa-l-Rashad 8/170: weak chain. The primary report contains the initial three requests, with minor variations.

Al-Tabarani, al-Muʿjam al-Awsat 9448

Component: The same first three requests, including the wording the day I meet You in it. Al-Haythami, Majmaʿ al-Zawa’id 10/160: narrators are those of the Sahih collections except al-Adhrami, who is trustworthy; this is a narrator assessment, not an explicit full-report sahih grading. The text occurs within a Bedouin’s prayer reportedly met with Prophetic approval. This is a separate report from the preceding citation.

Al-Tabarani, al-Muʿjam al-Awsat 661

Component: O Guardian of Islam and its people, keep me steadfast in it until I meet You. Al-Albani, al-Silsila al-Sahiha 1476: hasan chain. The primary excerpt contains thabbitni bihi hatta alqak, matching the printed recension.

The concluding Arabic as’aluka ʿanni wa-ʿan mawlay is present in the original source but its narrated source was not verified. The bracketed words follow the original Urdu explanation; the final Arabic clause is elliptical and its narrated source has not been verified. This edition follows the original Arabic wording.

Supplication85

Protection from affliction, misguidance and a harmful death

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from an evil life and trials of the heart. I seek refuge in Your might—there is no god but You—from Your letting me go astray, from severe affliction, the depths of misery, an adverse decree and the gloating of enemies; from the evil of what I have done and what I have not done; from the evil of what I know and what I do not know; from the loss of Your blessings, the withdrawal of the well-being You grant, the sudden onset of Your punishment and all Your displeasure;

from the evil of my hearing, my sight, my tongue, my heart and my semen; from destitution, from wronging others or being wronged, from a collapse falling upon me, from falling from a height, from drowning and burning; from Satan confounding me at the time of death; from dying while fleeing battle in Your cause; and from dying of a venomous bite.

Original commentary 85

In this supplication, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has mentioned thirty hardships and granted us the tremendous treasure of seeking Allah’s protection from every kind of calamity and affliction. For example, it teaches us to seek refuge from severe calamity, misfortune, the taunts of enemies, going astray, the loss of blessings, the reversal of well-being, destitution and so on. Above all, it teaches us to seek protection from Satan’s schemes and deceptions at the time of death. This prayer names such afflictions, calamities and troubles, and teaches us how to pray for protection from them, that no one could teach us in this way. May we be devoted to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: he mentions each of our sufferings and teaches us how to ask Allah for protection.

Sources and notesSunday · Prayer p. 55 · Composite with a disputed textual variant

Sunan Abi Dawud 1539

Component: A bad span of life and trials of the heart. Al-Albani: daʿif. The report narrates seeking refuge from su’ al-ʿumr and fitnat al-sadr. The book puts the narrated list into direct first-person prayer.

Sunan al-Nasai 5482

Component: Trials of the heart only. Darussalam: sahih. This stronger report independently supports fitnat al-sadr, but does not contain su’ al-ʿumr.

Sahih Muslim 2717

Component: Refuge in Allah’s might from being led astray. Sahih: included by Muslim in his Sahih. The printed phrase is an excerpt from Ibn Abbas’s longer prayer.

Sahih al-Bukhari 6616

Component: Severe affliction, misery, adverse decree and enemy gloating. Sahih: included by al-Bukhari in his Sahih. The report explicitly instructs seeking refuge from all four items.

Sahih Muslim 2716a

Component: Evil of what one has done and has not done. Sahih: included by Muslim in his Sahih. Both clauses are found together in Aisha’s report.

Sunan Ibn Majah 3846

Parallel only: Meaning of protection from evil known and unknown. Darussalam: sahih. The report asks refuge from all evil, immediate and deferred, known and unknown. It is a close semantic parallel, not verification of the exact short wording min sharri ma ʿalimtu wa-min sharri ma lam aʿlam.

Sahih Muslim 2739

Component: Loss of blessings, change in well-being, sudden punishment and all divine displeasure. Sahih: included by Muslim in his Sahih. The four clauses occur together verbatim.

Sunan Abi Dawud 1551

Component: Evil of hearing, sight, tongue, heart and semen. Al-Albani: sahih. The five body-related clauses are all present in the primary Arabic.

Sunan Abi Dawud 1544

Component: Poverty and wronging others or being wronged. Al-Albani: sahih. The report contains the justice clauses; it uses faqr for poverty, whereas the compilation has faqa.

Ibn Hibban 1030, reproduced in Abd al-Aziz al-Rajhi’s commentary

Component: The word faqa and wronging or being wronged. Included by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih; no separate chain grading verified here. The scholar’s transcript reproduces the primary report with its chain and faqr wa-l-faqa, followed by the two justice clauses.

Sunan Abi Dawud 1552

Component: Collapse, falling, drowning, burning, Satan at death, fleeing battle and a venomous bite. Al-Albani: sahih. The full final sequence is present, with the compilation omitting old age and repeated introductory phrases.

Al-Shawkani, Tuhfat al-Dhakirin, pp. 420–421

Component: The known/unknown wording as a recorded recension. Not independently assessed: al-Shawkani attributes this wording to a Nasai recension and Ibn Abi Shayba. The primary commentary explicitly distinguishes the known/unknown and done/not-done forms and discusses both. The underlying Nasai or Ibn Abi Shayba edition for the known/unknown reading was not independently located.

Al-Ghazali, Ihya ʿUlum al-Din 1/322, with al-Iraqi’s takhrij

Locator: 1/322, note 4. Component: The known/unknown wording and a textual reservation. Al-Iraqi identifies a copy/wording issue and says Muslim’s established wording is done/not-done. The devotional text contains known/unknown; the accompanying critical note distinguishes it from Muslim’s wording and mentions a separate mursal report with a related clause.

This long prayer is assembled from numerous reports, not one hadith. Most components have sound or favourably graded sources. The opening pair occurs in a weak report, although trials of the heart has independent sound support. The known/unknown form is recorded and attributed to Nasai and Ibn Abi Shayba by al-Shawkani, while al-Iraqi notes a textual problem and identifies Muslim’s reading as done/not-done. The known/unknown wording is therefore attested, while its underlying primary recension and authenticity remain unverified here. The Urdu on original printed page 45 supports the broad bad-life rendering of su’ al-ʿumr. Although the original commentary refers to one hadith, the numbered prayer is the compiler’s collection of transmitted protections.

ClosingDurood

O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet, and upon his family, and grant them peace in abundance.

Note from the Urdu edition

Recite Durood at the beginning and end of every manzil. This is a means for supplications to be accepted. (See page 64 of the original edition.)

Reference review

The source’s instruction is retained above. Praise and blessings before duʿā have support in Abu Dawud 1481; the weekly arrangement is the compiler’s. The specific eighty-year reward quoted with Monday’s Durood has not been established as sound. See general references G1 and G3.

General blessings upon the Prophet are supported by Qur’an 33:56. A general encouragement does not by itself establish a particular count, occasion or reward.
